rationale: All 19 acceptance criteria satisfied; one major functional gap found: 'Plugin' appears in the shared useAllIntegrationTypeOptions hook options (plugin key is in CREDENTIAL_UI_MAPPING) and is shown in the Workflow integration_type filter, but compose_workflow_integration_type_filter has no path to match Plugin-using workflows — Plugin is an INTERNAL_TOOLKIT excluded from the discoverable registry and has no PLUGIN_TOOL_NAMES constant (unlike Git). Selecting 'Plugin' in the Workflow filter triggers query.where(false()), silently returning 0 results for all workflows even when Plugin tools are present. All other blind-lens flags were dismissed: the delete newQuery.integration_type pattern is the standard URL-rebuild pattern (false positive), lru_cache and GIT_TOOL_NAMES are by-design and spec-documented, field_name indexing is an internal-contract convention, and jsonb_array_elements(null) is safe on PostgreSQL 15.

findings.problem: Plugin integration type silently returns 0 Workflow results
findings.impact: Users who select 'Plugin' in the Workflow integration_type Multiselect always see an empty workflow list. compose_workflow_integration_type_filter calls get_tool_names_for_credential_types(['Plugin']), which returns an empty set (Plugin is in INTERNAL_TOOLKITS so it is excluded from _credential_type_to_tool_names, and there is no PLUGIN_TOOL_NAMES constant analog to GIT_TOOL_NAMES). An empty tool_names triggers query.where(false()), filtering out every workflow. The FE shows this option because useAllIntegrationTypeOptions maps all CREDENTIAL_UI_MAPPING keys, which includes 'plugin'.
findings.recommendation: Exclude Plugin from Workflow filter options on the FE by filtering the result of useAllIntegrationTypeOptions in WorkflowsFilters (or creating a useWorkflowIntegrationTypeOptions variant that drops Plugin). Unlike Git, Plugin tool names are user-defined and cannot be enumerated in a static frozenset, so the fix is FE-only: do not offer an option the BE cannot honor.
